subject: Dedicated capacity plan and burst/autoscale agreement for QuantumCore launch

Subject: Dedicated capacity plan and burst/autoscale agreement for QuantumCore launch

Hi Anna —

Great chat this morning. I pulled together a concise plan for the Dedicated offering we discussed, focused on the initial launch window (Q3 feature rollout) and the first 90 days of expected ramp. Key asks so we can finalize sizing:

- Confirm 95th-percentile concurrent sessions and expected p50/p95 token throughput during the peak 2-hour window.
- Any hard latency SLOs for user-facing inference (e.g., <150ms p95 for short prompts)?
- Will you require synchronous GPU-backed embeddings pipelines at the same SLA, or can embeddings run as batch jobs?

Our provisional approach (see attached CSV with your May signals):
- Reserve: baseline slab sized for p95 steady-state (we've preliminarily estimated a 12-GPU slab).
- Burst: ephemeral headroom for product launches, mapped as a preemptible shoulder pool (up to +40% of baseline) for 8 weeks post-launch.
- Autoscale policy: target 60% utilization to trigger scale-up, cool-down 300s, with a rapid scale-down window for <15m transient spikes.
- Eviction and fallback: best-effort preemptible eviction policy, with routing fallback to a smaller, lower-cost model variant to maintain availability.

Next steps: Marcus and Priyom will sketch the initial dedicated-sizing doc, then we’ll schedule a call with your ops/procurement to lock timelines. Attaching the usage export you shared this morning.

Thanks,
Camila Reyes
Senior Account Lead, Redwood Inference

Thanks Camila — this aligns with what we discussed. A few clarifications from our side:

- Expected p95 concurrency during launch: ~1,200 concurrent sessions (sustained 15–30m bursts), baseline p95 token throughput ~18k tokens/sec across requests.
- Latency target: we want p95 <= 200ms for interactive short prompts; for longer batch jobs (embeddings) we can tolerate higher latency if routed to batch workers.
- Procurement timeline: we are aiming to finalize terms by 6/15 to get the slab provisioned by 7/1.

I'll ask procurement to share the standard PO flow and scope the security questionnaire. We'll need an ops working session next week to confirm routing fallbacks and model-variant mappings.

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity plan and burst/autoscale agreement for QuantumCore launch

Folks — attaching my initial draft sizing sketch based on Anna's numbers and the May export. High-level proposal:

1) Baseline slab: 12x A100-equivalent GPUs (reserved) to meet p95 steady-state for the first 90 days.
2) Shoulder pool: ephemeral +5 GPUs (preemptible) available for automated burst during launch windows; policy to permit up to +40% headroom for up to 2 hours, with a persistent ephemeral allowance for 8 weeks.
3) Autoscaler tuning: scale-up trigger when average GPU utilization across slab >60% for 2 consecutive 5-minute buckets; scale target in 2-GPU increments to avoid overshoot. Scale-down after sustained <35% for 10 minutes, plus a 300s cool-down.
4) Preemption handling: on eviction, route short interactive traffic to a quantized model variant (approx -20% quality, -45% cost) hosted in a fallback pool; background embedding workloads can run to completion on batch nodes.
5) Canary & rollout: start with 20% of traffic on dedicated slab for the first 24h, increase to 60% over 72h if no errors/regressions. Toggleable fallback to hosted API during extreme congestion.

I added 'eviction_safety_brief' notes in the attached PDF. This covers our suggestion for monitoring alerts and a temporary crediting approach if preemptions materially impact user experience (we discussed one-time launch credits).

Attachment: dedicated-sizing-draft-v1.pdf

Marcus
Sr. Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity plan and burst/autoscale agreement for QuantumCore launch

Anna — appreciate the quick responses and the timelines. Summarizing agreed items and next actions so we have a single source of truth: 

Agreed: 
- Baseline reserved slab: 12 GPUs (A100-equivalent) to cover p95 steady-state.
- Shoulder (preemptible) pool: +5 GPUs available for automated burst; up to +40% headroom for 2h launches, ephemeral allowance 8 weeks.
- Autoscale policy: scale-up at avg util >60% (2x5m buckets), cool-down 300s, scale-down after sustained <35% for 10m.
- Eviction fallback: routing to quantized model variant + batch routing for embeddings.
- Canary: 20% traffic -> 60% -> full over 72h if green.

Next steps: 
1) Marcus to finalize the dedicated-sizing PDF and add concrete alert thresholds and escalation contacts (ETA: Mon 6/4).
2) Camila & QuantumCore ops to run the routing/fallback runbook in a 60-min tabletop on Tue 6/6 (I'll send invite).
3) Procurement to share PO language; procurement@quantumcore.com to confirm by 6/12.
4) Security: we received a SOC2 snapshot request (Anna, I've attached the requested bundle).
